turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to wrap my head around the ARMADA paper we discussed last week. Specifically, what is FLOAT exactly?
FLOAT is an autonomous online failure detection method featured in ARMADA. It helps identify issues in real-time without manual intervention.
Got it. Does it require a lot of computational overhead to run that detection?
It's designed to be lightweight, but the exact overhead depends on the frequency of the checks you configure.
Okay, noted. By the way, did my order for the mechanical keyboard switches arrive yet?
Let me check... No, it still says 'In Transit'. It should arrive by Friday.
Cool. I'll keep an eye out. Thanks for the info on FLOAT.
You're welcome. Let me know if you need more details on ARMADA.
Lloyd, I finally got around to cleaning up the codebase today. I replaced the custom replay logic in the Alfie GR00T server.
That's a good move. What did you replace it with?
I used ReplayPolicy. It seems to handle the state management much more cleanly than our old ad-hoc scripts.
ReplayPolicy is indeed more robust for that server. Did you update the documentation as well?
Not yet. I'll get to it after dinner. I'm thinking of trying that new Thai place downtown.
Sounds delicious. Do you want me to check if they have reservations available tonight?
Yes, please. And remind me to commit the ReplayPolicy changes before I head out.
I've added it to your reminders. Reservation request sent for 7:30 PM.
